added.title: Director of Engineering
added.description:
Powercast is seeking an experienced Director of Engineering
to lead, scale, and inspire our engineering team. In this role, you will bridge technical vision and business strategy. You will manage cross-functional engineering teams spanning electrical, mechanical, embedded systems, and firmware engineering—taking complex hardware products and semiconductor chips from initial architecture and prototyping through to high-volume design for manufacturing and commercial production.

Key Responsibilities

Engineering Leadership & People Management: Manage, mentor, and grow project managers and team leads across EE, ME, Firmware, and Test. Build an inclusive, high-performing culture centered on design robustness, quality, safety, and structured operational execution.
Product Strategy & Cross-Functional Alignment: Partner with product management, industrial design, operations, and supply chain to align product roadmaps with business goals. Balance aesthetic, performance, cost (BOM), and manufacturability requirements.
Technical Architecture & System Design: Oversee high-level system architecture, component selection, and design for excellence (DFX/DFM/DFA). Ensure products comply with global regulatory standards (FCC, CE, UL, RoHS) and meet strict reliability targets.
Process & Operational Excellence: Implement hardware development cycles (gates, design reviews, testing, and V&V protocols) to increase release predictability and product quality.
Resource & Budget Management: Allocate lab equipment, prototyping resources, and capital expenditures.

Qualifications

Experience: 10+ years of hardware engineering experience, with 5+ years in senior management roles (managing managers and multidisciplinary teams) in a fast-paced hardware or consumer electronics tech company.
Technical Depth: Deep background in board-level electrical design, mechanical architecture, embedded firmware/software systems, and prototyping techniques.
Manufacturing Savvy: Hands-on experience bringing high volume (1M+) physical hardware to market through EVT, DVT, and PVT stages, including working directly with domestic and overseas manufacturing partners.
People First: Proven track record of recruiting, mentoring, and retaining top engineering talent across multiple disciplines.
Communication: Exceptional ability to translate complex hardware engineering tradeoffs (e.g., cost vs. performance vs. schedule) to non-technical stakeholders and executive teams.

Preferred Qualifications

Prior experience scaling a hardware organization through high-growth product launches or expanding product portfolios.
Deep knowledge of supply chain risk management, custom tooling, and vendor qualification processes.
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or equivalent field.

MBTA’s core values are built around safety, service, equity, sustainability, culture, and accessibility, and each employee that works for the MBTA performs their roles based on our vision, mission, and values. This includes attendance, participation, and contribution in local safety committee meetings as needed.

Job Summary

The Director of Software Engineering is responsible for ensuring quality custom software development by managing software engineering operations, process, standards and rituals. The Director of Software Engineering manages a team practicing adapted Agile development in a DevOps environment. Currently, all infrastructure is infrastructure-as-code hosted in Amazon Web Services (AWS); almost all software is written in Elixir. The Director of Software Engineering encompasses technical management, operational planning, mentorship and growth, culture development, internal stakeholder management, internal project management, and ensuring adherence to modern software development principles.

Ensure the software engineering function for the department is reliable, secure, and responsive to the needs of internal teams.
Ensure the software engineering standards are documented and communicated throughout the function.
Work closely with the software engineering infrastructure teams to ensure compliance with process and data controls.
Document and share the software engineering operating model.

Manage the financial processes for the engineering function, including reviewing financial statements for accuracy, participate in developing pro forma, inform operating budget, support development of capital improvement project budgets, and approve budgeted procurements.
Provide leadership, guidance, and direction to Deputy Directors, Technical Leads, and senior engineering managers.
Oversee and establish best practices for people management, including retention, hiring, and performance management for the engineering function.
Collaborate with other projects and programs on joint recruitment efforts.
Support the professional development of direct reports and junior staff, including individual contributors and technical leads, helping them navigate their challenges, and ensuring they have the necessary skills and resources. Foster collaboration between different functional groups ensuring that technical staff work effectively with product managers, researchers, writers, and designers.
Inform and incorporate strategic plan goals into team processes, monitor status of action items and report status to stakeholders within the department and across the authority.
Define and articulate standards for software engineering and technology is developed to enhance public service delivery.
Oversee risk mitigation through quality assurance programs and compliance with MBTA policies.
Investigate and report incidents related to safety or quality concerns to appropriate departments.
Partner with MBTA Information Security to maintain compliance and observability standards.
Refine internal policies in line with security best practices and cloud/software development standards.

Seven (7) years of experience in agile software development environment.
Five (5) years of supervisory, managerial, and/or leadership experience.
Experience with 2+ programming languages from the TIOBE top 20.

Experience with APIs / microservices / Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA).

At LinkedIn, our approach to flexible work is centered on trust and optimized for culture, connection, clarity, and the evolving needs of our business. LinkedIn's Data Center Engineering organization is responsible for the strategy, design, construction, deployment, operations, and continuous evolution of the infrastructure that powers LinkedIn's global platform. We are seeking a Senior Director of Data Center Engineering to lead a multidisciplinary organization responsible for data center operations, construction and delivery, infrastructure lifecycle management, capacity growth, and critical facilities engineering across a global portfolio.

This leader will provide strategic direction and operational leadership for LinkedIn's data center infrastructure, ensuring world-class reliability, scalability, efficiency, and cost effectiveness. The role requires a blend of executive leadership, technical expertise, program execution, and business acumen to support LinkedIn's rapidly growing compute and AI infrastructure demands.

The ideal candidate has extensive experience leading hyperscale, enterprise, or colocation data center environments and is capable of driving outcomes across engineering, operations, finance, real estate, sourcing, capacity planning, and executive leadership teams. Responsibilities align closely with LinkedIn's current Data Center Engineering portfolio, including operations, design and delivery, provider management, long-term capacity strategy, and advanced cooling initiatives.

Lead global data center operations, engineering, construction, and delivery functions across multiple regions.

Develop organizational priorities, operating models, staffing plans, and investment strategies to support business growth.

Serve as the executive point of contact for data center providers, strategic partners, and senior leadership stakeholders.

Drive innovation across data center design, operational excellence, sustainability, automation, and AI infrastructure readiness.

Data Center Design & Construction

Establish and maintain engineering standards, Basis of Design (BOD) documents, commissioning requirements, and operational readiness processes.

Lead crisis management and executive response during critical infrastructure incidents and service-impacting events.

Ensure facilities operate at peak efficiency while maintaining LinkedIn's resiliency and reliability standards.

Capacity, Provider & Business Management

Partner with Capacity Planning, Hardware Engineering, Networking, and Infrastructure organizations to align infrastructure delivery with future demand.

Lead relationships with colocation providers, contractors, equipment vendors, consultants, and service partners.

Drive lease negotiations, provider governance, business reviews, expansion planning, and commercial decision-making.

Develop annual operating and capital budgets and ensure disciplined execution against financial targets.

Prepare business cases for major investments, infrastructure upgrades, and strategic initiatives.

People Leadership

Lead and develop a high-performing team of managers, engineers, and technical leaders.

Build a culture centered on safety, accountability, operational excellence, inclusion, and continuous learning.

Establish succession plans, talent development strategies, and career growth opportunities across the organization.

Foster strong cross-functional partnerships and alignment across engineering, operations, real estate, sourcing, finance, security, and legal teams.

Emerging Technologies

Lead the evaluation and deployment of next-generation data center technologies, including high-density compute environments and direct liquid cooling solutions.

Drive innovation in monitoring, automation, telemetry, sustainability, and operational efficiency.

Stay informed of industry trends and ensure LinkedIn remains at the forefront of data center engineering practices.

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Construction Management, or a related technical field.

15+ years of experience in data center engineering, operations, construction, or critical infrastructure environments.

7+ years of experience leading engineering, operations, or construction teams.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field.

Experience managing large-scale data center infrastructure programs across multiple facilities or regions.

Demonstrated expertise in mission-critical electrical and mechanical infrastructure systems.

Experience managing multimillion-dollar capital and operating budgets.

Experience leading vendor, contractor, and colocation provider relationships.

Strong executive communication and stakeholder management skills.

Experience with site selection, colocation strategy, lease negotiations, and provider governance.

Experience with liquid cooling, AI infrastructure deployments, and high-density compute environments.

Strong understanding of commissioning, integrated systems testing, and operational readiness processes.

Experience driving large-scale organizational transformation, standardization, and operational improvement programs.

Global Product Technology (GPT) delivers the platforms and capabilities that power lululemon’s product lifecycle – from 2D/3D design and development to merchandising, sourcing, assortment planning, master data management, and go to market. You’ll collaborate closely with the mobile, firmware, and backend engineers on the team, product managers, designers, and the leadership team to plan and deliver new features, ensure system reliability, and evolve our cloud architecture. You’ll also help guide technical strategy, mentor teammates, and elevate engineering standards across the organization.

Leadership & Management

Lead a team of 7 engineers (FTE + Contract).
Estimate work efforts, collaborate on requirements, and plan dev sprints in coordination with Product leadership.
Participate in the strategic direction of the company in collaboration with the rest of the Senior Leadership team.

Backend Engineering

Architect, build, test, deploy, and maintain backend features and services.

At Vanta, our mission is to help businesses earn and prove trust. We believe that security should be monitored and verified continuously, and we empower companies to practice better security and prove it with ease. Vanta's Corporate Engineering team is the infrastructure layer that keeps 1,500+ people connected, secure, and moving fast. AI is now central to how that happens, and this role leads the team that owns the backbone underneath it.

Corporate Engineering owns the shared AI platform for Vanta's internal systems: identity and access for AI tools, cost visibility and controls, sanctioned tooling and guardrails, and the enablement that helps people use those tools well. We do not own product AI, which stays with Engineering, and we do not replace the AI work happening inside individual departments. We build the engineering layer that makes all of it safer, cheaper, and better supported.

The company has moved fast. AI assistant use is widespread across every function, MCP infrastructure is live and self-serve company-wide, internal apps ship on a hosted platform, and AI spend has grown to the point where attribution and guardrails genuinely matter. What does not exist yet is a single owner for that platform layer. That is this role.

As Sr. Manager, AI Engineering, you will lead a small, senior team, write the charter for what Corporate Engineering owns versus enables, and build the platform that lets the rest of Vanta adopt AI quickly without accumulating cost, risk, or duplication.

What you’ll do as a Senior Manager, AI Corporate Engineering at Vanta:

Lead, coach, and grow a senior team spanning platform engineering and technical program management. Set clear direction, hold a high bar, and give the team explicit permission to push back with data.
Own the AI access layer end to end: identity and authentication for AI tools, connector and integration allowlisting, tiered permissions by function, and guardrails that make adoption safe by default rather than safe by exception.
Own AI cost engineering. Build attribution down to team and individual, right-size model selection to actual need, make agent and automation spend traceable, and set budget thresholds and alerting in partnership with Finance.
Own the MCP layer for internal tools end to end, including commissioning, decommissioning, governance, and the downstream impact assessment that has to happen before a migration ships rather than after it breaks.
Own the paved path for internal applications: a golden-path deployment pattern, sensible defaults including private-by-default, lifecycle and decommissioning policy so unused apps retire themselves, and a build-versus-buy framework that keeps people from rebuilding tools we already own.
Build the enablement layer that turns adoption into impact: a skills and agent registry that cuts duplication, an evaluation framework for internal AI usage, and technical enablement on sanctioned tools that goes beyond provisioning access.
Write and hold the charter. Define what Corporate Engineering owns, what it enables, and how work enters the team, then convene the cross-functional forum that keeps departmental AI efforts coordinated rather than duplicated.
Partner across Engineering, GRC, Security, Data, Finance, and People. Several of the levers this role depends on sit in those organizations, so the job is to coordinate and influence rather than override.

Experience standing up an internal AI or developer platform function rather than inheriting a mature one. You have written the charter, defined intake, and built the roadmap from a blank page.

Hands-on technical depth across LLM platform tooling, agent and MCP architecture, identity and OAuth, CI/CD, and infrastructure as code. Enough to review a design honestly and tell the difference between real risk and reported progress.
Comfort building for an audience that is no longer only engineers. A growing share of the people shipping internal tools are not developers, and the platform has to work for them without lowering the security bar.
Data governance fluency in a regulated environment. You know what should never enter a prompt, a repository, or a third-party tool, and you can make that judgment fast without becoming the bottleneck.
Comfort operating through influence. Product AI, security policy, data platform, and budget authority all sit in partner organizations.
8+ years in platform, infrastructure, or systems engineering, including 3+ years managing and developing engineers, ideally at a company that scaled through a significant headcount inflection.
Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for current or future employer sponsorship.
Open to using AI to amplify their skills and strengthen their work, demonstrating curiosity, a willingness to learn, and sound judgment in applying AI responsibly to improve efficiency and impact.

What you can expect as a Vanta’n:

Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, with 100% of employee-only benefit premiums covered for most medical plans
16 weeks paid Parental Leave for all new parents

We started in 2018, in the wake of several high-profile data breaches. Online security was only becoming more important, but we knew firsthand how hard it could be for fast-growing companies to invest the time and manpower it takes to build a solid security foundation. Vanta was inspired by a vision to restore trust in internet businesses by enabling companies to improve and prove their security. Our Ethos

We believe in an open and flat structure. You will be able to grow into the role that most aligns with your goals. Our team members at all levels have the freedom to explore ideas and impact the roadmap and vision of our company.

About The Team

We are hiring a Head of Engineering to own the craft, quality, and technical direction of a roughly 30-person engineering organization. This is deliberately not a role about growing headcount to 150. It is a role about making a small, senior team produce output that looks like a much larger one — by raising the engineering bar, tightening the systems that move real money, and being genuinely in the code and the architecture rather than adjacent to it.

You will lead through a mix of direct reports and a small group of engineering managers and tech leads, partnering closely with Product, Risk, and Compliance. You will spend your time on design reviews, incident retros, hiring, and the handful of technical bets that determine whether we can support the next order of magnitude of transaction volume.

If your ideal week is entirely calendar blocks and roadmap decks, this is not the right role. If your ideal week includes a hard design debate, a code review that changes someone's mind, and a coaching conversation that raises a manager's ceiling, keep reading.

Set and own Rain’s engineering quality bar across system design, code review, testing, observability, documentation, and technical decision-making, ensuring correctness is treated as critical for systems that move customer funds.
Provide hands-on technical leadership by staying active in the codebase, reviewing critical PRs and designs, prototyping high-risk components, debugging production issues, and making key architectural and build-vs.-buy decisions.
Own the technical architecture and strategy across card issuing, wallets, ledger, money movement, onchain settlement, and integrations with card networks and banking partners.
Drive reliability, scalability, and operational excellence by establishing SLOs, improving incident response, capacity planning for 10x growth, and designing resilient systems with graceful degradation, idempotency, and replay capabilities.
Build security, compliance, and correctness into the platform by design, partnering closely with Risk, Compliance, and Security to meet PCI, SOC 2, fraud-control, regulatory, and blockchain infrastructure requirements.
Increase engineering velocity without sacrificing quality through improvements to CI/CD, developer tooling, local environments, technical debt management, and architecture that enables teams to ship safely and independently.
Build and develop a high-performing engineering organization by coaching engineering managers and technical leads, maintaining a high hiring and performance bar, establishing clear team ownership, and partnering effectively across Product, Design, Risk, Compliance, and GTM.

You Are Likely To Succeed If You Have

10+ years building production software, including 4+ years leading engineers — ideally as a Head of Engineering, Director, or Senior EM at a company where the systems handled real consequences.
Currently and demonstrably hands-on. You have written or reviewed meaningful production code within the last year and you want a role where that continues.
Deep experience with distributed backend systems at scale: data modeling, consistency and idempotency, queues and event-driven design, and the operational reality of running all of it.
A track record of raising an engineering bar. You can point to specific practices you introduced and the measurable change in quality, velocity, or reliability that followed.
Real reliability ownership — you have carried a pager, run incident command during a serious outage, and built the follow-through that kept it from recurring.
Experience in payments, fintech, banking infrastructure, or another domain where money, ledgers, or regulatory obligations made correctness non-negotiable.
Strong hiring and coaching instincts, with managers or senior engineers you have developed who would work for you again.
Clear written communication. You can make a complex technical tradeoff legible to a CEO, a compliance officer, and a partner's engineering team in the same week.
Comfort with ambiguity and speed. You would rather ship something correct this quarter than design something perfect for next year.

Bonus Attributes

Hands-on experience with card issuing, processing, or the Visa and Mastercard network stack.
Working knowledge of stablecoins, onchain settlement, custody and key management, or EVM and Solana infrastructure.
Experience operating under SOC 2, PCI DSS, or bank and program-manager oversight.
Experience leading distributed or multi-region teams.

About The Company

Rain is the global stablecoin payments platform for enterprises, neobanks, platforms, developers, and AI agents. Our technology allows partners to move, store, and use stablecoins instantly and compliantly through global payment cards, rewards, on/offramps, wallets, and cross-border rails. As both a Visa and Mastercard Principal Member, Rain issues cards that work at more than 175 million merchant locations in over 220 countries and territories. Built natively for stablecoins and trusted by more than 100 organizations worldwide, Rain delivers secure, scalable infrastructure that makes money move freely and instantly around the world.

You will have the opportunity to deliver massive impact at a hypergrowth company backed by some of the top investors in fintech, crypto, and SaaS. In January 2026, we closed a $250M Series C led by ICONIQ, valuing Rain at $1.95B, with Sapphire Ventures, Dragonfly, Bessemer Venture Partners, Galaxy Ventures, FirstMark, Lightspeed, Norwest, and Endeavor Catalyst also participating. If you're curious, bold, and excited to help shape a borderless financial future, we'd love to talk.

Our Ethos

We believe in an open and flat structure. You will be able to grow into the role that most aligns with your goals. Our team members at all levels have the freedom to explore ideas and impact the roadmap and vision of our company.

About The Team

We are hiring a Head of Engineering to own the craft, quality, and technical direction of a roughly 50-person engineering organization. This is deliberately not a role about growing headcount to 150. It is a role about making a small, senior team produce output that looks like a much larger one — by raising the engineering bar, tightening the systems that move real money, and being genuinely in the code and the architecture rather than adjacent to it.

You will lead through a mix of direct reports and a small group of engineering managers and tech leads, partnering closely with Product, Risk, and Compliance. You will spend your time on design reviews, incident retros, hiring, and the handful of technical bets that determine whether we can support the next order of magnitude of transaction volume.

If your ideal week is entirely calendar blocks and roadmap decks, this is not the right role. If your ideal week includes a hard design debate, a code review that changes someone's mind, and a coaching conversation that raises a manager's ceiling, keep reading.

What You’ll Do

Own engineering strategy and architecture across card issuing, wallets, ledger, money movement, onchain settlement, and integrations with card networks and banking partners — including the multi-year technical roadmap that gets us there.
Set and own Rain's engineering quality bar across system design, code review, testing, observability, documentation, and technical decision-making, ensuring correctness is treated as critical for systems that move customer funds.
Go deep where the risk is. You won't own day-to-day code, but you will review critical designs, weigh in on the highest-consequence architecture and build-vs.-buy decisions, and be technical enough that no one can hand you a bad design and have it pass.
Drive reliability, scalability, and operational excellence by establishing SLOs, improving incident response, capacity planning for 10x growth, and designing resilient systems with graceful degradation, idempotency, and replay capabilities.
Build security, compliance, and correctness into the platform by design, partnering closely with Risk, Compliance, and Security to meet PCI, SOC 2, fraud-control, regulatory, and blockchain infrastructure requirements.
Increase engineering velocity without sacrificing quality through improvements to CI/CD, developer tooling, local environments, technical debt management, and architecture that enables teams to ship safely and independently.
Build and develop a high-performing engineering organization by hiring and coaching engineering managers and technical leads, establishing clear team ownership and boundaries, and owning headcount planning and the performance bar.
Operate as a member of the leadership team — translating company strategy into technical plans, partnering across Product, Design, Risk, Compliance, and GTM, and representing engineering to the board, banking and network partners, and customers.

You Are Likely To Succeed If You Have

15+ years building production software, including 8+ years leading engineers and meaningful time leading managers.
Current technical credibility. You have written or reviewed meaningful production code recently enough that an architecture review is a place you add value, not a place you nod along.
Deep experience with distributed backend systems at scale: data modeling, consistency and idempotency, queues and event-driven design, and the operational reality of running all of it.
A track record of raising an engineering bar. You can point to specific practices you introduced and the measurable change in quality, velocity, or reliability that followed.
Real reliability ownership — you have carried a pager, run incident command during a serious outage, and built the follow-through that kept it from recurring.
Experience in payments, fintech, banking infrastructure, or another domain where money, ledgers, or regulatory obligations made correctness non-negotiable.
You have hired and developed engineering managers, not only engineers. There are leaders you grew who would come work for you again.
Clear written communication. You can make a complex technical tradeoff legible to a CEO, a compliance officer, and a partner's engineering team in the same week.
Executive range. You are as comfortable in a board or partner conversation as you are in a design review, and you can hold a technical position under commercial pressure.
Comfort with ambiguity and speed. You would rather ship something correct this quarter than design something perfect for next year.

Bonus Attributes

Hands-on experience with card issuing, processing, or the Visa and Mastercard network stack.
Working knowledge of stablecoins, onchain settlement, custody and key management, or EVM and Solana infrastructure.
Experience operating under SOC 2, PCI DSS, or bank and program-manager oversight.
Experience leading distributed or multi-region teams.

Job Description

Make an impact
. Our teams design and build advanced electronics that protect those on the front lines—from detecting threats for F‑35 pilots to illuminating the night for soldiers. Spanning air, land, sea, and space, we deliver tomorrow’s technology today. We draw strength from our differences and innovate for the future. You can, too.

Why BAE Systems

Our flexible work environment helps you do meaningful work without compromising your life outside of work. Our mission is simple and profound: We Protect Those Who Protect Us®. Join us.

About The Role

BAE Systems is seeking a Deputy Director to lead microelectronics engineering and foundry operations for a high‑visibility portfolio. You will steer strategy, execution, and continuous improvement across design, fabrication, packaging, and production for programs totaling $100M+ annually.

What You’ll Do

Lead & Grow a High-Performing Team: Direct and mentor a team of skilled engineers and manufacturing professionals operating our 6-inch (150mm) wafer fabrication facility. Focus on creating a safe, high-quality environment where innovation thrives.
Drive Innovation from Design to Production: Lead the full lifecycle of microelectronics component development - from initial design and fabrication through packaging and into large-scale production for both development and deployed programs.
Be a Strategic Partner: Collaborate closely with Business Area leadership, providing critical insights and ensuring projects stay on schedule, within budget, and meet stringent performance requirements.
Chart the Course for Future Success: Develop and champion a sector-level microelectronics capability roadmap, leveraging both internal expertise and insights from external leaders in the field.
Ensure Operational Excellence: Establish and maintain best-in-class operating policies and procedures, aligned with company standards and regulatory compliance.
Manage & Optimize: Drive budget and resource planning, setting key performance indicators (KPIs) for financial performance, staffing, yield, quality, and delivery. Identify and implement improvements to optimize operations, reduce costs, and accelerate production timelines.

What You'll Bring

Proven Leadership: A demonstrated track record of successfully operating and managing advanced semiconductor chip manufacturing facilities in a production environment.
Technical Expertise: Deep understanding of advanced process technologies, particularly within GaAs/GaN fabrication.
Strategic Thinking: Ability to synthesize complex information, develop forward-looking roadmaps, and translate strategy into actionable plans.
Problem-Solving Skills: Ability to analyze complex challenges, develop creative solutions, and implement effective strategies.
Strong Communication Skills: Ability to effectively communicate with both technical and non-technical audiences, including senior leadership.
Results-Oriented: A proven ability to deliver results in a fast-paced, demanding environment.
Growth Mindset: A commitment to continuous learning, embracing new technologies, and fostering a culture of innovation within the team.

Required Education, Experience, & Skills

Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Materials Science, Physics, or related field; 15+ years in microelectronics with 10+ years leading wafer fab and packaging operations.
U.S. citizenship with eligibility to obtain a Secret security clearance.
Proven experience leading large organizations of engineers, technicians, and program staff.
Demonstrated success planning, managing, and executing complex projects.
Exceptional communication, collaboration, and stakeholder management skills.
Passion for mentoring mid‑ to late‑career team members; proven talent development results.

Preferred Education, Experience, & Skills

Director‑level leadership in microelectronics (commercial or defense), especially in III–V technologies (GaAs/GaN), RF/MMIC, advanced packaging, and high‑reliability manufacturing.

Full-Time Salary Range: $173023 - $294137

Please note: This range is based on our market pay structures. However, individual salaries are determined by a variety of factors including, but not limited to: business considerations, local market conditions, and internal equity, as well as candidate qualifications, such as skills, education, and experience.

Regular employees scheduled to work 20+ hours per week are offered: health, dental, and vision insurance; health savings accounts; a 401(k) savings plan; disability coverage; and life and accident insurance. BAE Systems, Inc. is the U.S. subsidiary of BAE Systems plc, an international defense, aerospace and security company which delivers a full range of products and services for air, land and naval forces, as well as advanced electronics, security, information technology solutions and customer support services. Working here means using your passion and ingenuity where it counts – defending national security with breakthrough technology, superior products, and intelligence solutions. Exploiting every electron, we push the limits of what is possible, giving our customers the edge and our employees opportunities to change the world. Our products and capabilities can be found everywhere – from the depths of the ocean to the far reaches of space. At our core are more than 14,000 highly talented Electronic Systems employees with the brightest minds in the industry, we make an impact – for our customers and the communities we serve.

Own the delivery of cloud platform and infrastructure capabilities across multiple initiatives, ensuring alignment with business, mission, and security requirements
Set and guide technical direction for Azure Government platforms, ensuring solutions are scalable, secure, and operationally sustainable
Establish and evolve DevSecOps practices and automation approaches to improve delivery consistency, quality, and reliability
Make informed technical and delivery trade off decisions, balancing speed, quality, security, risk, and long term platform health
Lead architecture and design efforts, reviewing and approving solutions to ensure alignment with standards, constraints, and desired outcomes
Oversee risk, dependency, and issue management across delivery efforts, escalating and resolving proactively as needed
Influence stakeholders across product, engineering, and leadership teams to align priorities and drive execution without direct authority
Develop and grow engineering talent through coaching, feedback, and delegation, strengthening overall team capability
Promote operational excellence by continuously improving processes, tooling, and ways of working

Skills And Attributes For Success

Demonstrates accountability for outcomes, taking ownership of decisions and following through to execution
Applies sound judgment when operating in ambiguity, making trade offs that consider delivery impact, risk, and long term sustainability
Influences outcomes across teams and stakeholders through credibility, collaboration, and clear communication
Communicates complex technical and delivery topics effectively to technical, business, and executive audiences
Adapts approach as priorities, constraints, and requirements evolve while maintaining delivery momentum
Develops people and teams by providing clear direction, timely feedback, and opportunities for growth
Promotes a culture of quality, risk awareness, and continuous improvement
Demonstrates curiosity and continuous learning, staying current with evolving technologies, delivery practices, and firm direction

To qualify for the role, you must have

7+ years in engineering roles working with private/public cloud IaaS, PaaS, and/or SaaS
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, IT, or equivalent experience
Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate (AZ-104) and Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect Expert (AZ-305)
Strong hands-on experience:
Infrastructure as Code & CI/CD – designing and delivering with tools such as Bicep, Azure DevOps, ARM templates, or Ansible
Containers and orchestration – experience building and running containerized workloads using technologies such as Docker, Kubernetes, Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), Azure Container Apps, or Helm for packaging and deploying services at scale
Networking fundamentals – strong foundation designing and troubleshooting VNets, subnets, network security groups (NSGs), routing (UDRs), and basic load-balancing scenarios, with enough depth to reason about hub-and-spoke or similar topologies and diagnose common connectivity issues
Cloud security principles – solid understanding of concepts such as shared responsibility, least privilege, identity-driven security, network segmentation, encryption, and logging/monitoring, and how to apply them for customers driven by regulatory compliance requirements, such as: NIST, FedRAMP
Identity and access – understanding of Microsoft Entra ID, Azure RBAC, Entra ID RBAC, Privileged Identity Management (PIM), and managed identities for Azure resources
Windows and Linux administration – hands-on experience managing, troubleshooting, and hardening server workloads, including patching, performance tuning, and applying security baselines (e.g., DISA STIG or equivalent)
Scripting / programming – practical automation experience using PowerShell (Python or similar scripting languages is a plus but not required
Experience with government security frameworks (e.g., NIST controls)
Hands-on delivery in Agile environments (Scrum, Kanban, SAFe, or similar)
Strong written and verbal communication and the ability to work effectively on distributed teams

Ideally, you’ll also have

Ability to obtain and maintain Top-Secret Security Clearance
Deeper hands-on experience with:
Git-based source control and branching strategies
AWS/GCP cloud experience / knowledge
Azure DevOps Pipelines and broader Azure platform services
Ansible and Bicep for advanced automation and configuration
Azure Policy and multi-tenant / multi-subscription design patterns
Advanced Azure networking experience – hands-on exposure to one or more of: VPN Gateway or ExpressRoute, Azure Firewall or other NVAs, Virtual WAN hubs, Application Gateway or similar L7 gateways, and more complex hybrid or multi-region network designs

Additional relevant certifications, such as:
AZ-400, AZ-500, AZ-700
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) or CKAD / CKNS
Red Hat Certified Specialist in Ansible Automation

A self-starter, independent-thinker, curious and creative person with ambition and passion
History of continuous learning and continuous progression
